overview: The two main sections of the intestine, split by their primary role — nutrient digestion/absorption versus water absorption and waste formation.
genZNote: Small intestine: where the real digestion and nutrient pickup happens. Large intestine: where leftover water gets reclaimed and waste gets packaged.

aspects.label: Main Function
aspects.valueA: Completes digestion and absorbs most nutrients (glucose, amino acids, fats).
aspects.valueB: Absorbs water and electrolytes, and forms/stores faeces.

aspects.label: Length vs Diameter
aspects.valueA: Longer (about 6-7 metres) but narrower in diameter.
aspects.valueB: Shorter (about 1.5 metres) but wider in diameter.

aspects.label: Surface Adaptation for Absorption
aspects.valueA: Lined with villi and microvilli, greatly increasing surface area for absorption.
aspects.valueB: Lacks villi; absorption is mainly of water via simple diffusion.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Despite being called 'large', the large intestine is actually shorter in length than the small intestine — the name refers to its greater diameter, a common exam trick.
overlay.memoryTrick: Small intestine = small diameter, does the real digestive work. Large intestine = large diameter, mostly water recovery.
overlay.commonMisconception: Very little actual digestion happens in the large intestine — its main jobs are water absorption and faeces formation, not breaking down nutrients.
